cells.tense: Right now the hours go in without being forced into a shape first.
cells.act: break the habit that was propping it
cells.ask: Name a routine you keep. Skip it once, on purpose. See what leans on it, then decide whether it comes back.
cells.core:
The grip here is loose. You can put in the hours without the hours turning into a wall, and the repeating still feels like a direction you chose rather than a guard you posted. Refinement serves the work, not the worry.

An ending you have been avoiding can land cleanly, because nothing has hardened around it yet. Drop a habit you have kept past its use and watch what the day fills the gap with. Craft and mere chafing get told apart by the break. The ground stays open underneath either way, and you are free to find you would rather keep the habit — that counts too. Nothing comes down that was carrying anything. What comes down was propping something already standing.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the hours without being kept by them.
cells.verb: practicing before the shape is chosen
cells.place: the open ground where nothing has settled into form yet

cells.tense: Soon a morning will come when pausing feels like losing ground you cannot get back.
cells.act: surrender the outcome and keep the act
cells.ask: Take the work once more, then set it down at an ending you did not choose — the act kept, the result left alone.
cells.core:
Practice has to be finished before it can be trusted, and untested work reads as a threat. Solitude that once felt chosen feels required, and each session exists to hold off a failure that has not arrived. Nothing gets to be partial. Nothing gets to be a draft.

So let one thing end on purpose. Stop a session at a point you did not pick, put the work down, and walk off — not abandoned, just released. That is the mechanism doing its own job, not a loss. The version you have now is the version; the next pass costs more than the last one gained. What looked like the edge of the work turns out to be the end of the sentence. Pick it back up tomorrow and nothing irreparable has bent in the night.

cells.tense: Time was when practice was the room the body learned to keep away from.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: Weigh an hour of practice against what else that hour carries — sleep, a friend, food — set both sides level, and quit adjusting once they match.
cells.core:
The hours were spent somewhere and none of them stuck. The body learned to keep its distance from the thing, and the distance held. A small steady light that used to go somewhere sits unused, and no one has asked why.

Stop trying to force the hours back. Weigh what practice asks of you against what else that hour carries — sleep, a friend, food — and set the two sides where they look level, then leave the scale alone. In proportion, the hour thins to something the week can hold without bending. Fairness does the work here; effort pushed into the starved place only proves it starved again. When the share is true, the old resistance stops finding anything to push against.

cells.tense: There is a hand already moving in the room and no one has said whose it is.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Carry out the smallest piece of what keeps happening for you, then jot one line about it — what you did, what it cost. Notes only; no claim attached.
cells.core:
You are getting good at something without having watched it happen, or you are steering clear of the thing and calling the steering clear a preference. Either way the hours are already being spent somewhere, and it is you who is spending them.

Don't force the picture to arrive. Do one small piece of what keeps happening, then put a line on paper about it. The line is the whole of the act — not a plan, not a resignation, not a claim about who you now are. What you have already lived is enough to begin from. A year from now turns out to be a tally of small lines, and the fog does not have to lift for the next step to be the obvious one.
